newsitem.title: USA: New cos spun from General begin trading.
newsitem.headline: New cos spun from General begin trading.

text.p: Three new public companies that emerged from the strategic reorganization of General Instrument Corporation began trading on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) on Monday.

The companies were NextLevel Systems Inc, a company which supplies systems and components for high-performance communications networks; CommScope Inc, manufacturer of coaxial cable and supplier of high-performance electronic cables and General Semiconductor Inc, a company which deals with power rectifiers and voltage suppressors, began trading on the NYSE on Monday.

The last day of trading shares in General Instrument was July 25 1997. As of Monday, for each outstanding share of General Instrument stock, stockholders received one share of NextLevel Systems, one-third share of CommScope and one-quarter share of General Semiconductor.
